Hi Jake — thanks for the clear worksheet. I did a quick pass with Product and Assurance and put together a proposed operational playbook below; attaching a clean redline with inline comments (draft-exhibit-redlines.docx).

Proposed evidence rhythm (pragmatic):
- SOC 2: annual report delivered to HapinCare via NDA within 10 business days of request; rolling 12-month attestation access to latest SOC 2 report in Drive (PDF).
- Monthly: summary token-level noise/usage dashboard (export) for the prior 30 days — automated export.
- Quarterly: evidence bundle (config snapshots, retention summaries, patching cadence) delivered as a zipped manifest.

Pen-test / staging:
- We propose a 2-week staging window after an agreed notice (30 days recommended) for customer-initiated tests.
- Production testing is generally disallowed; exceptions require: a) signed Restart Plan, b) a mutually-agreed allowlist for scanner IPs, c) 48-hour emergency rollback SLA.

Inspection / audit rights:
- Redwood can provide bounded inspection (sampled instance access) with pre-approved scopes; live interactive forensics only with a mutual NDA and authorized personnel list.
- For sensitive logs/data, we propose redaction guidance and a shortform attestation to avoid exporting raw user data.

Operational asks from our side:
- Please confirm whether your SOC 2 access will be via an internal portal link or central mailbox so we can set up automated delivery.
- Confirm the list of HapinCare reviewers that require full bundles vs. summary artifacts.

Next steps / timeline suggestion:
1) Legal redline pass (we'll provide) — by 05/27 — Laura will lead.
2) Technical evidence sample — Redwood to deliver sample bundle by 06/03 — Marissa to own.
3) Pen-test scheduling — target window the week of 06/23 if contract signed by 06/16.

If acceptable I'll push the redline into DocuSign and flag the order-form changes.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Dylan / team — quick legal read and proposed edits. I attached a marked-up document (legal_comments_redlines.docx). High-level suggestions:

1) Inspection clause: change from open "inspection rights" language to a bounded inspection: we should propose sampling (no more than 3 non-consecutive days per 12-month period) and require a minimum of 21 days' notice. This protects our multi-tenant ops while being reasonable.

2) SOC 2 access: provide access copies of the latest SOC 2 report under NDA; do not grant raw log export rights. Add language that allows Redwood to redact customer-specific identifiers in evidence bundles.

3) Pen test carveouts: allow customer testing only in staging + ephemeral test accounts. For production testing, require a written waiver and a documented rollback/communications plan; require the customer to perform non-destructive testing and to supply a signed attestation of scope.

4) Escalation & credits: add a mutually-agreed process for SLA credit requests tied to failure to deliver committed evidence (we can accept a capped credit, but need the legal path defined).

Operational notes for Product/Assurance:
- We should provide Marissa with a one-page sample evidence bundle template and an internal runbook that maps evidence items to owners.
- Ask: can Product add an allowlist feature for a temporary scanner IP list? If not, we will need the Order Form to state exceptions are at Redwood's discretion.

I'll be available for a 30-min sync today 3–3:30pm PT if that helps.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — helpful notes. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The 21-day inspection notice is acceptable; however, HapinCare needs the option for a 48-hour high-priority evidence request in incident scenarios (we'd treat that as exception handling with limited scope).
- For SOC 2 access: we typically need a rolling 12-month window; a single PDF is not enough for procurement. We can accept redacted bundles, but we need the ability to validate scope coverage (assertions map).
- Pen-test: we can agree to staging-only, but HapinCare asks that the scheduling window be committed within 60 days of signature — we need predictability for our internal timelines.

We attached an evidence wishlist that maps items to our internal risk categories. Also: if Redwood requires a capped credit for missed evidence, please propose numbers in the redline so we can evaluate tradeoffs.
